evidence.notes: Built fresh -> MIX -> HTR (outlet 400 K) -> SPL (0.2 purge / 0.8 recycle) -> REC -> MIX with SteamTables. dof_check: fresh is under-specified (missing 2 of T, P, vapor fraction), so solve() was not run and there are no residuals.

infeasible.reason: under-specified: missing fresh water temperature and pressure (dof_check: feed 'fresh' needs 2 more of T, P, vapor_fraction). T_mixed_K depends on the fresh water's temperature, and the pressure decides whether the 400 K recycle is liquid or steam.

evidence.notes: Peng-Robinson; feed 100 mol/s C1/C2/nC5/nC7 70/10/10/10 at 290 K, 20 bar into a two-phase separator (vap, liq). VF_feed read from the feed stream, y_CH4 from vap, x_C7 from liq. Max residuals: mass 2.4e-5, compound 5.8e-5, energy 2.4e-5 (relative).

Rigorous column (40 stages, feed on 30, R=10, D=40.625 mol/s by mass balance) at 1 atm with NRTL failed to converge. Separate bubble-point scan of the feed flash (NRTL, 101325 Pa) shows a minimum-boiling azeotrope at x_EtOH≈0.87, T≈351.530 K (vs 351.545 K at 0.90 and 351.691 K at 0.97); the scan flowsheet's verifier flagged ok=false only because of a heater left half-built by a failed add_unit call and a 0.17% energy residual on the valve.

infeasible.reason: Distillate spec of 0.97 mol frac ethanol is beyond the ethanol-water minimum-boiling azeotrope at 1 atm (NRTL: x_EtOH≈0.87, T_bub≈351.53 K). Ordinary distillation of a 0.40 feed cannot take the top past ~0.87, so the rigorous column fails to converge and no D/R_min exists for this split.

evidence.notes: Built feed (water, SteamTables, 20 kg/s, 300 K, 5 bar) -> pump P1 (outlet 3 bar, eta 75%). Solve ok, mass residual 0, energy residual 3.4e-9, but pump duty = -5.35 kW (negative) and T_out = 299.98 K: the device would be producing work, not using it.

infeasible.reason: Pump discharge pressure (3 bar) is below the suction pressure (5 bar), so dP = -2 bar. A pump cannot lower pressure; DWSIM returns a negative shaft power of -5.35 kW, which is expander/turbine behaviour. Use a valve or a discharge pressure above 5 bar.

evidence.notes: Built a single adiabatic compressor K1 (PR, 100 mol/s, 85/7/4/2/2 % C1/C2/C3/nC4/CO2, 300 K, 10 bar in, outlet_P 5 bar, eta 75 %). DWSIM solved it as an expansion: duty -207.98 kW, outlet 244.13 K. Max residuals: mass 0, energy 4.6e-8.

infeasible.reason: Compressor discharge pressure (5 bar) is below the inlet pressure (10 bar). A compressor cannot consume power to lower pressure: the simulator returns negative work (-207.98 kW) and cooling to 244.1 K, i.e. expander behaviour. Use an expander, or set a discharge pressure above 10 bar.

evidence.notes: heat_exchanger_area (counter-current) raised a temperature cross: hot-end ΔT = 350-360 = -10 K, cold-end ΔT = 300-320 = -20 K. Each side simulated separately as a heater/cooler (SteamTables, 1 bar): Q_hot = 2091.15 kW vs Q_cold = 1340.03 kW, energy residuals ~1e-9.

infeasible.reason: Temperature cross in a counter-current exchanger: cold outlet 360 K > hot inlet 350 K (ΔT1 = -10 K) and hot outlet 300 K < cold inlet 320 K (ΔT2 = -20 K), so no positive LMTD or finite UA exists. The four fixed temperatures are also over-specified: the hot side gives up 2091.15 kW but the cold side needs only 1340.03 kW (IAPWS-IF97).

evidence.notes: Built FEED (100 mol/s, 85/7/4/2/2 % C1/C2/C3/nC4/CO2, 300 K, 50 bar, PR) and outlets A, B. DWSIM rejected the splitter: 'Split ratios must sum to 1; they sum to 1.2'. dof_check confirms A and B have no producing unit. No solve was possible.

infeasible.reason: Mass balance violated: split fractions 0.70 + 0.50 = 1.20 > 1, so A + B would be 120 mol/s from a 100 mol/s feed. DWSIM rejects ratios that do not sum to 1.

evidence.notes: Built 10 kg/s water at 300 K, 2 bar (SteamTables / IAPWS-IF97) feeding a heater with outlet_T_K=350 and heat_added_kW=500. dof_check: over-specified (mutually exclusive outlet_T_K and heat_added_kW). Check copy with only T_out=350 K solved ok=true (energy residual 5.5e-9) and gave a required duty of 2091.0 kW, not 500 kW.

infeasible.reason: over-specified: the heater has both an outlet temperature (350 K) and a duty (500 kW). A heater accepts only one of them, and they disagree: reaching 350 K needs 2091.0 kW (solved with only the temperature spec), not 500 kW.

evidence.notes: Built PR flowsheet fs1 (feed 100 mol/s at 17 bar, VF=0, 5/45/40/10 % C2/C3/nC4/nC5; product and Qc/Qr streams). The simulator refused to add shortcut_column COL with 'missing required param reflux_ratio'; dof_check afterwards showed no units added and also flagged the feed as missing one state variable although P and VF=0 were given (likely a tool quirk). No solve was run.

infeasible.reason: under-specified: missing the column's operating reflux ratio (or R/Rmin, or a stage count). With the key specs (2 % nC4 in distillate, 2 % C3 in bottoms) and the pressures (16/17.5 bar), FUG fixes only Nmin and Rmin; N and Qr depend non-linearly on R, and the simulator would not create the column without reflux_ratio.

evidence.notes: Built feed gas_in (100 mol/s, 300 K, 10 bar) -> adiabatic compressor K1 (75 %, outlet 30 bar), Peng-Robinson. dof_check: gas_in under-specified, missing composition; K1 ok. Not solved because that would require inventing a gas composition.

infeasible.reason: under-specified: missing the composition of the 'process gas' feed (mole fractions or component flows). Compressor power and discharge temperature depend on it non-linearly through heat capacity, gamma and Peng-Robinson real-gas behaviour; dof_check reports gas_in as under-specified.

evidence.notes: Built a PR flowsheet: feed 100 mol/s at 230 K (C1 0.80, C2 0.08, C3 0.04, nC4 0.02, nC5 0.02, N2 0.02, CO2 0.02) feeding a separator with vapor and liquid products. The specification check failed: feed missing 1 more of (T, P, vapor_fraction). No solve was run because the card gives no pressure.

infeasible.reason: under-specified: missing the flash pressure. The card fixes only T = 230 K and the flow; VF and y_CH4 at 230 K depend strongly and non-linearly on pressure, and the specification check reports the feed needs one more of (P, vapor_fraction).

evidence.notes: Mixer with steam tables (IAPWS-IF97): 100 kg/s water at 300 K + 50 kg/s at 350 K, both at 2 bar. The solve converges (mass residual 0, energy 4.7e-11) with the outlet at 316.68 K and 150 kg/s. Specification check passes without the 340 K; imposing it would be one spec too many.

infeasible.reason: over-specified: an adiabatic mixer's outlet temperature comes from the energy balance, so it cannot also be fixed. The balance gives T_out = 316.68 K (F_out = 150 kg/s), not the 340 K imposed (about 23 K apart); reaching 340 K would need added heat, which contradicts 'adiabatic'.

evidence.notes: Pure CH4 feed 100 mol/s at 300 K (Peng-Robinson) into a flash separator. Solve at 50 bar ok (mass error 0, energy error 9e-10); pressure varied 1-500 bar at 9 points: liquid flow 0 mol/s at every point, never reaches the 30 mol/s target.

infeasible.reason: Liquid demanded above the critical temperature: methane Tc ≈ 190.6 K (Pc ≈ 46 bar) < 300 K, so pure methane is supercritical and forms no liquid at any pressure. The DWSIM flash gave 0 mol/s liquid at every pressure from 1 to 500 bar, so no pressure gives 30 mol % liquid and there is no liquid density.

evidence.notes: Built an adiabatic mixer (SteamTables / IAPWS-IF97) fed 100 kg/s water at 300 K and 50 kg/s water at 350 K, both at 2 bar. The solve converged and the balances closed (largest error 4.7e-11). The product stream P came out at 150 kg/s, 316.68 K, 2 bar, all liquid; these numbers are for reference only and do not answer the requested 200 kg/s case.

infeasible.reason: Mass balance violated: the product of a mixer with no reaction must equal the sum of its inlets, 100 + 50 = 150 kg/s. The required 200 kg/s would create 50 kg/s of mass. The simulator gives 150 kg/s at 316.68 K.

evidence.notes: Conversion reactor (PR, isothermal 298.15 K, 101325 Pa), feed 1 mol/s CH4 + 9.52 mol/s N2, reaction CH4 + 2 O2 -> CO2 + 2 H2O at 100% CH4 conversion. Solved ok: mass residual 0, energy residual 1.9e-8. Outlet CO2 ~1e-10 mol/s, CH4 unreacted, duty ~-8e-8 kW.

infeasible.reason: Reactant missing: the feed has 0 mol/s O2, but 100% conversion of 1 mol/s CH4 needs 2 mol/s O2. The 9.52 mol/s N2 is the nitrogen of stoichiometric air without its oxygen. DWSIM gives zero extent: CO2 ~1e-10 mol/s, duty ~-8e-8 kW, all CH4 unreacted. The 100% conversion spec cannot be met.

evidence.notes: Built a shortcut column in DWSIM (Peng-Robinson): saturated-liquid feed 100 mol/s at 17 bar, keys propane/n-butane, 2 % / 2 % specs, condenser 16 bar, reboiler 17.5 bar, R = 0.6. Solve failed with the column's own error: 'Defined Reflux Ratio (0.6) lower than calculated minimum (1.2807)'. No balances, because the column did not calculate.

infeasible.reason: Reflux below minimum: the specified R = 0.6 is less than the R_min = 1.281 that DWSIM calculated for the 2 % nC4 in distillate / 2 % C3 in bottoms separation. At R < R_min no number of stages reaches the specs (N goes to infinity), so neither N nor the condenser duty exists.

evidence.notes: Built feed (100 mol/s, 300 K, 10 bar, PR) -> Valve V1 (outlet_P = 20 bar). DWSIM computed an isenthalpic outlet T of 305.84 K (dT = +5.84 K), mass err 0, energy err 8.6e-10, but that result is a non-physical artifact: a valve cannot raise pressure.

infeasible.reason: Valve asked to raise pressure: outlet 20 bar > inlet 10 bar. An isenthalpic throttling valve can only lower pressure (flow goes from high to low P with no work input); raising the pressure needs a compressor.

evidence.notes: DWSIM SteamTables cooler: 8 kg/s water 360->320 K at 3 bar, duty read from the cooler E1 = 1339.89 kW; mass residual 0, energy residual 3.8e-8. heat_exchanger_area with shell_passes=1 (1-2, Fakheri F), cooling water 300->315 K, U=850 W/m2K.

No units, so no balance residuals to check.

Feed of 100 mol/s at 300 K and 50 bar (85/7/4/2/2 C1/C2/C3/nC4/CO2) goes through valve V1 set to 10 bar outlet; isenthalpic expansion, Peng-Robinson. T_out_K is read from the valve outlet stream 'out' (274.7796 K), dT = T_out - 300. Max residuals: mass 0, compound 1.7e-16, energy 4.3e-11. Vapour fraction is 1 at inlet and outlet.
